definition: Specialized computer hardware is often used to execute artificial intelligence (AI) programs faster, and with less energy, such as Lisp machines, neuromorphic engineering, event cameras, and physical neural networks.
details: Since 2017, several consumer grade central processing units (CPUs) and systems on a chip (SoCs) have on-die neural processing units (NPUs). As of 2023, the market for AI hardware is dominated by graphics processing units (GPUs), such as those by Nvidia and AMD, newer domain-specific accelerators such as Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), and various NPUs found in consumer hardware.

explainer.lead: Hardware for artificial intelligence is computer equipment designed to run AI programs efficiently. It matters because specialized processors can often perform the same work faster and with less energy than general-purpose hardware.

tiers.eli5: A regular computer processor is like an all-purpose kitchen knife, while AI hardware can be like a tool made for one repeated cutting job. That special tool can often finish the job more quickly and use less energy. Examples include special chips inside consumer devices and larger processors used to run AI programs.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run AI workloads on GPUs from vendors such as Nvidia and AMD, domain-specific accelerators such as Google's TPUs, or NPUs integrated into consumer CPUs and SoCs. The practical goal is faster execution, lower energy use, or both, rather than assuming every workload will benefit equally. As of 2023, GPUs dominated the AI hardware market alongside these newer accelerators and consumer NPUs.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, AI hardware is specialized computer hardware H used to execute AI programs, with the objective of reducing execution time T and/or energy consumption E relative to less specialized execution. Its forms include Lisp machines, neuromorphic engineering, event cameras, physical neural networks, GPUs, TPUs, and NPUs. The definition describes potential efficiency gains, not a guarantee for every program or device.

explainer.example: A consumer SoC with an on-die NPU can use that neural processing unit to execute an AI program instead of relying only on its general-purpose CPU, with the aim of running it faster or with less energy.

explainer.intuition: General-purpose processors handle many kinds of tasks, while specialized AI hardware is built to execute AI programs more efficiently. The intended payoff is greater speed, lower energy use, or both.
howItWorks: An AI program is assigned to suitable computer hardware.
A specialized device, such as a GPU, TPU, or NPU, executes the program.
Its specialization is intended to reduce execution time or energy use.
The hardware may be a separate accelerator or an NPU integrated on the same die as a consumer CPU or SoC.
explainer.whyItMatters: Specialized hardware makes efficient AI execution possible across both consumer devices and larger accelerator-based systems. It also shapes the AI hardware market, which GPUs dominated as of 2023.
misconceptions: AI hardware means only GPUs: it also includes TPUs, NPUs, neuromorphic engineering, event cameras, and other forms.
NPUs exist only in large systems: several consumer CPUs and SoCs have included them since 2017.
Specialization always guarantees improvement: the defining aim is faster or more energy-efficient execution, not a universal guarantee.
